plan.topic: Orforglipron's third Phase 3 trial, now peer-reviewed: ATTAIN-J in Japanese adults with obesity disease (238 randomized, 72 weeks, double-blind vs placebo; Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol, Oct 30, 2026)
plan.angle: Title: 'Orforglipron Pill: What the Japan Trial Confirms'. Open within 10 s: 'In a 72-week trial in Japanese adults with obesity disease, orforglipron cut weight by up to 8.7% on average, compared with 0.6% on placebo.' Then give each arm with its n (6 mg −5.9%, n=61; 12 mg −8.7%, n=57; 36 mg −7.9%, n=60; placebo −0.6%, n=60), and say plainly that the highest dose didn't give the most loss. Use the measure the paper names. Define obesity disease: BMI 27 or higher plus type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure or high cholesterol. Add one line on why this matters: in many Asian populations, obesity-related conditions show up at lower BMI. Add ATTAIN-1 (12.4% vs 0.9%, if everyone stayed on treatment, adults without diabetes, 72 weeks), marked 'separate trials, not head-to-head'. US status: FDA approved 1 Apr 2026 for chronic weight management. Give the Japan or EU status only if verified on publish day. Add one per-arm nausea line from the paper. Close with the don't-switch line, 'Not personal advice' and the prescriber line. Never call it the 'third' Phase 3 trial.
plan.working_title: Orforglipron Pill: What Its Third Phase 3 Trial Confirms #shorts
plan.why: The full paper came out Oct 30 and pill interest is rising. This deliberately replaces the 13:00 retatrutide/head-to-head slot: TRANSCEND-T2D-2 already had a Short this week, and an insulin head-to-head would repeat the 10-30 template. It can feed the orforglipron long-form (202 min). | fact-check: ATTAIN-J exists. It was published in Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol (https://www.thelancet.com/journals/landia/article/PIIS2213-8587(26)00232-9/abstract; registry NCT05931380, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05931380). Design: 238 randomized 1:1:1:1 (6 mg n=61, 12 mg n=57, 36 mg n=60, placebo n=60). Population: Japanese adults with obesity disease, defined as BMI ≥27 with type 2 diabetes, hypertension or dyslipidaemia. At 72 weeks, weight change was −5.9% / −8.7% / −7.9% vs −0.6% on placebo. Three issues. (1) The top dose did not give the largest loss: 12 mg (−8.7%) beat 36 mg (−7.9%). Leading with 'the top dose arm' would hide that and imply a dose-response the trial didn't show. Report all three arms, or say 'up to 8.7% with the 12 mg dose'. (2) 'Third Phase 3 trial' is not accurate. Orforglipron already has several peer-reviewed Phase 3 trials (ACHIEVE-1, ATTAIN-1, ATTAIN-2, ACHIEVE-J and others). Drop 'third' from the title and script. (3) I could not confirm the 30 Oct online date or which estimand the headline uses (the publisher returned 403). Content_check must confirm both before the '48 h / fresh' framing is used. Also, ATTAIN-1's 12.4% vs 0.9% is the 'if everyone stayed on treatment' figure (36 mg, adults without diabetes, 72 weeks), so label it that way and match the ATTAIN-J measure, or state that the measures differ. Verified US status: FDA approved Foundayo (orforglipron) for chronic weight management on 1 Apr 2026. The loop and 'what's confirmed?' format is fine. Avoid the dose numbers being heard as dosing advice: say 'three doses tested' and present them only as trial arms.

factcheck.summary:
The script is accurate and safe to ship. I found no major problems, only two minor wording fixes.

Checked against ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05931380 (results posted 20 Jul 2026):
- **Arms and results:** 238 people randomized. Placebo had n=60 and −0.63%. 6 mg had n=61 and −5.90%. 12 mg had n=57 and −8.69%. 36 mg had n=60 and −7.93%. All were measured at week 72 and all doses beat placebo (p<0.001). The script's 8.7, 5.9, 7.9 and 0.6 match.
- **Who was eligible:** BMI 27–34 with 2 or more obesity-related problems, or BMI 35+ with 1 or more. At least one problem had to be high blood pressure, high cholesterol or type 2 diabetes. That matches s3.
- **Publication:** The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology article exists (online 30 Oct 2026). Its summary says side effects were mostly mild-to-moderate stomach problems, which supports s7.
- **ATTAIN-1:** The NEJM PubMed record (online 16 Sep 2025) confirms 3,127 adults without diabetes. Counting everyone who started, 36 mg gave −11.2% versus −2.1% on placebo at 72 weeks, which matches s6.
- **FDA:** The FDA Novel Drug Approvals 2026 page lists Foundayo (orforglipron), approved 1 Apr 2026. The indication is adults with obesity, or overweight plus at least one weight-related condition, alongside a reduced-calorie diet and more physical activity. That matches s8.
- **Asian BMI:** The WHO Expert Consultation (Lancet 2004;363:157–163) supports the line about higher health risks at lower BMI. The PubMed page didn't load on fetch, but the citation is the standard, well-known record.

Framing checks:
- s5 keeps the 12 mg vs 36 mg point honest: small groups, doses not compared directly.
- s6 says "separate trials, not head-to-head".
- No dosing advice. The don't-switch/stop/change line, "Not personal advice" and the prescriber line are all there.
- The narration is exactly 170 words, which is at the limit.

The two minor fixes:
1. ATTAIN-J included some people with type 2 diabetes (about 25%, per the trial registry), and the script never says so.
2. The planning note says both trials "counted everyone who started", but I couldn't open the paywalled Lancet text to confirm how ATTAIN-J counted its results. That wording should stay out of any ATTAIN-J text.

issues.claim: "Japanese adults with obesity disease". In s6 this is set next to ATTAIN-1, "adults without diabetes".
issues.problem: ATTAIN-J included people with type 2 diabetes (about 25% of participants, per the ClinicalTrials.gov eligibility section), and the script never says so. A viewer could take the s2/s6 contrast as two populations that differ only by country. The playbook asks for the trial population everywhere.
issues.fix: In s3, change the last sentence to: "Some had type 2 diabetes. Many Asian populations face higher health risks at lower BMIs." To stay at 170 words or fewer, cut "here" from s3 ("Obesity disease meant BMI twenty-seven or higher…") and "on average" from s2. If you cut "on average", put it back in the s2 stat label: "ATTAIN-J, Japanese adults (some with type 2 diabetes): 12 mg vs placebo −0.6%, 72 weeks, average".

issues.claim: "Like-for-like context: both trials counted everyone who started."
issues.problem: The registry describes ATTAIN-J's numbers as model-based estimates for all randomized participants, with missing values filled in statistically. That fits "counting everyone who started", but I couldn't open the paywalled Lancet text to confirm it. Nothing spoken or on screen makes this claim for ATTAIN-J, so it shouldn't move into captions or descriptions.
issues.fix: Leave s2 as it is. Don't add "counting everyone who started" to any ATTAIN-J caption or description line. In the metadata, change the hook_pattern clause to: "Like-for-like context: ATTAIN-1 figure counts everyone who started; separate trials, not head-to-head."
